literal: Women of public charm's / base charm / they will not embrace / by goodness of mind / glorious / those of wisdom.
translation: Those whose wisdom is made glorious by the goodness of their mind will not embrace the base charms of women who offer their charms to all.
modern: சிறந்த அறிவும் நல்ல மனமும் உடையவர்கள், பொருள் கொடுப்பவர் அனைவருக்கும் பொதுவான இன்பம் தரும் மகளிரின் அற்பமான இன்பத்தை நாட மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: The couplet contrasts two kinds of 'goodness' or 'charm' (நலம்). The women offer a 'public charm' (பொதுநலம்) which the poet calls a 'base charm' (புன்னலம்). In contrast, the wise possess the 'goodness of mind' (மதிநலம்) which makes their wisdom glorious. Because their minds are elevated, they will not degrade themselves by seeking the cheap, transactional affection of prostitutes.
